_comment: What is DECLARED to ship, per deficiency and per surface. verify_shipped.py checks the source files against this, so the decision is explicit and reviewable rather than inferred from which transform files happen to exist on disk.

protan.reason: v2 REJECTED on visual review. It passed all five held-out metric checks, but costs 14% more distortion on realistic content and still loses to daltonize on rescue, gain and safe palettes. Protanopia is an open problem.

deutan.reason: v2 SHIPPED. Rescue 0.718-0.777 -> 0.851-0.896 on held-out simulators, leading the field ahead of daltonize, at equal lattice fidelity. Costs 34% more distortion on realistic content, judged worth it for that margin.

tritan.reason: v2 SHIPPED. Best result in the benchmark: wins the metrics, halves damage to already-safe palettes (-9.5 -> -4.2), and is the only matrix LESS distorting on realistic content than the one it replaces. Known caveat: washes the low end of a red-green ramp toward white for a tritan viewer.

desktop_app.reason: DELIBERATELY ON v1. MagSetFullscreenColorEffect applies the matrix to gamma-encoded sRGB, while every browser surface applies it in linear light. Measured consequence: deutan rescue 0.731 (linear) vs 0.696 (sRGB) under Brettel 1997; tritan 0.810 vs 0.877. The v2 matrices were derived in linear space, so shipping them here would be an unmeasured change. The desktop app needs its own sRGB-space derivation.
